articles.headline: 'The Hoop Collective': Episodes of Brian Windhorst's NBA podcast
articles.description: Here are the top highlights from Brian Windhorst's "The Hoop Collective" podcast, from breaking news to the latest intel and reaction from around the NBA.
articles.body:
"The Hoop Collective" podcast, hosted by ESPN's Brian Windhorst, releases episodes every Monday, Wednesday and Friday during the NBA season and Tuesday and Friday during the offseason. Windhorst and his guests break down what's happening on and off the court, evaluating the trends you need to know and examining the latest news from across the NBA.

ESPN | Spotify | YouTube | Apple | Amazon | iHeartMedia | TuneIn

'The Hoop Collective' episodes

Sept. 22: Extensions that deserve more attention

Brian is joined by ESPN's Tim MacMahon to cover the substantial extensions that flew under the radar this offseason and some future deals to keep an eye on. They close on financial bonuses that separate the Los Angeles Lakers and New York Knicks with the rest of the league.

MacMahon on Jalen Duren's contract standoff with Detroit: "There has never ever been a player with anything close to the credentials that Duren has, an All-Star third team all NBA, a damn near 20 and 10 guy for the No. 1 seed in the Eastern Conference. There's never been a guy in that kind of a situation who signed for the qualifying offer. The closest comp you can get to that is actually another Pistons big man. It was Greg Monroe, but it was completely different circumstances."

Windhorst on a potential Brandon Miller extension in Charlotte: "I think if it's a five-year deal, I think you're looking for that. If it's a five-year deal, I think you're looking if you're him, you want that first number to be a two. Maybe right around two, but I'm sure that's probably what he's looking for. So, keep an eye on that."

articles.headline: Expected fantasy points (xFP): 2026 leaderboard for QBs
articles.description: xFP focuses solely on opportunity. Here are the leaders for 2026.
articles.body:
Expected fantasy points (xFP) strip away player talent and efficiency and focus solely on opportunity.

FORP -- fantasy points over replacement player -- is the difference between a player's actual fantasy point total (FF Pts) and his xFP (expected total).

Quarterback adjustments are made as follows:

Pass attempts: No change

Pass completions: Pass attempts multiplied by a passer's expected completion percentage based on depth of throw, location and target position

Passing yardage: Pass attempts multiplied by a passer's expected yardage based on depth of throw, location and target position

Passing touchdowns: Passing xTD

Interceptions: Pass attempts multiplied by a passer's expected interceptions based on depth of throw, location and target position

Rushing attempts: No change

Rushing yardage: Rush attempts multiplied by a rusher's expected yardage based type of rushing attempt

Rushing touchdowns: Rushing xTD

Two-point conversions: xTD multiplied by the league average two-point rate

Fumbles lost: Touches multiplied by the league average rate

articles.headline: NFL expected touchdown (xTD) leaderboard for 2026
articles.description: Opportunity-adjusted TD leaders tell you not only who's scoring but who's getting the opportunities to score.
articles.body:
What is xTD?

xTD stands for expected touchdowns. It is a statistic that weighs every carry/target and converts the data into one number that indicates a player's scoring opportunity. For example, if a player has an xTD of 3.0, it means that a statistically league-average player who saw the same number of carries/targets in the same area of the field would have scored three touchdowns.

xTD key

Looks = Carries + targets

TD = Actual TD total

xTD = Expected TD total

Diff = Difference between the player's total xTD and actual TD total

In5 = Carries by the player inside the opponent's 5-yard line

EZ = End zone targets

articles.body:
NBA Rank is back! With less than one month until opening night, let's start counting down the league's best players for 2026-27.

How many rookies landed in our top 100? Which stars who changed teams this summer are climbing our rankings? Where will the defending champion New York Knicks check in?

Our countdown begins with players Nos. 100-51 and continues Wednesday with Nos. 50-11 and Thursday with our expert panel's predictions for this season's top 10.

And that expert panel has been overhauled for the 2026 edition.

In previous seasons, more than 100 ESPN NBA insiders, reporters, editors and producers voted on thousands of possible player vs. player matchups to arrive at the final top-100 list.

That "wisdom of the crowd" approach has given way to the wisdom of seven: ESPN's Ben Golliver, Vincent Goodwill, Zach Kram, Bobby Marks, Dave McMenamin, André Snellings and Matt "Stats" Williams. (The panelists' individual top-100 lists were combined to create our final rankings.)

Voting guidelines, however, remained unchanged. The panel was asked to rank players based on predicted contributions -- quality and quantity -- for the 2026-27 regular season only.

Let's get to the list.

Note: Signature stats provided by ESPN Research.

100. Luguentz Dort

G | Atlanta Hawks

Age: 27

2025 NBA Rank: 64

The Dorture Chamber heads southeast, where the Hawks will be downright scary on the wings with Dort, Jalen Johnson and Dyson Daniels. Dort is still one of the league's most physical defenders and is entering the final year of his contract (at $18.2 million), so he'll be motivated in a new environment. His 3-point shooting fell off last season after two years at a 40% clip with the Thunder. Even if last season was a regression to the mean, the physicality Dort brings is the sell for the Hawks. -- Vincent Goodwill

Signature stat: Dort defended 2026 All-Stars for 1,238 matchups last season, the third most in the NBA.

Fantasy projection: 9.6 PTS, 3.8 REB, 1.0 STL

99. RJ Barrett

G | Toronto Raptors

Age: 26

2025 NBA Rank: 100

Barrett, the No. 3 pick in the 2019 draft, is a reliable secondary scorer who creates advantages with downhill attacks and plays well off lead options. Though the Toronto native hasn't developed into a franchise wing because of his mediocre outside shot and limited defensive impact, he thrilled his hometown fans in May with the signature moment of his seven-year career. When Barrett bounced home a last-second 3-pointer to beat the Cavaliers and force Game 7 in the Raptors' first-round playoff series, fans indulged in their most raucous celebration since the 2019 championship parade. -- Ben Golliver

Signature stat: Barrett shot 64% on layups and dunks last season, best in a season in his career and up from 55% in 2024-25, per GeniusIQ tracking.

Fantasy projection: 19.7 PTS, 5.6 REB, 3.9 AST

98. Jalen Suggs

G | Orlando Magic

Age: 25

2025 NBA Rank: 59

articles.headline: Red Sox agree to deals with manager Chad Tracy, Craig Breslow
articles.description: The Red Sox have named Chad Tracy as their full-time manager while also keeping chief baseball officer Craig Breslow in the fold, with both agreeing to long-term deals.
articles.body:
The Boston Red Sox have named Chad Tracy as their long-term manager while also opting to keep chief baseball officer Craig Breslow in the fold.

Tracy, who has guided the Red Sox to the postseason with a 74-55 mark as interim manager, agreed to a three-year deal as manager through the 2029 season with a club option for 2030.

Boston exercised its 2029 and 2030 options on Breslow.

"Craig and Chad are two exceptionally talented leaders who have earned these opportunities in very different ways," Red Sox president Sam Kennedy said in a statement. "Over the last three years, we have watched Craig bring clarity, discipline, and conviction to the work of building our baseball operation. Chad was asked to step into a difficult situation with little notice, but the trust he immediately commanded at the major league level was earned through years of work across our organization.

"What this team has accomplished over the past several months has been historic. Results matter greatly in this business, but so do judgment, character, and the ability to bring out the best in others. Craig and Chad have demonstrated all of those qualities, and they have earned our confidence in leading us forward."

The Red Sox, after getting off to a 10-17 start this season, handed the interim managerial reins to Tracy, 41, following the dismissal of Alex Cora on April 26. Two months later, on June 24, Boston was 32-46 and 15½ games back in the AL East. 

The team took off afterward, including a 27-3 run from July 3 to Aug. 7 -- the best 30-game span in franchise history.

The Red Sox are the fourth team to make the playoffs after being 14-or-more games under .500 in a season in the World Series era (since 1903). Two of the three previous instances made the World Series, with the Boston Braves winning it in 1914.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Real Madrid conspiracy claims dismissed as a 'smokescreen' by LaLiga president
articles.description: LaLiga president Javier Tebas has called claims of a refereeing conspiracy against Real Madrid "a smokescreen to hide other shortcomings" after the team's defeat to Atletico Madrid in Sunday's derby.
articles.body:
LaLiga president Javier Tebas has called claims of a refereeing conspiracy against Real Madrid "a smokescreen to hide other shortcomings" after the team's defeat to Atletico Madrid in Sunday's derby.

Coach José Mourinho said Madrid were denied "two clear red cards" in the game at the Metropolitano -- bringing a printout of photos of the incidents to his post-match news conference -- and alleged referee Miguel Ortiz Arias "couldn't cope with the pressure" of the high-profile fixture due to a lack of experience.

"I don't want to say this was prepared -- I want to think they were mistakes," Mourinho said, after a result which left Madrid six points behind Barcelona in the title race, adding that "if they let us compete on an even playing field, there's a long way left."

Tebas, who has frequently clashed with Madrid and club president Florentino Perez, commented on the debate on social media on Tuesday, while sharing an article which claimed "Real Madrid's enemies" were responsible for the team's struggles in LaLiga.

"The usual mouthpieces and the regime-aligned media are already spinning the same old narrative: the permanent conspiracy, Tebas posted on X. "When it isn't the Negreira case, it's the referee; or else, the complaint is that the official isn't an international-level referee."

"To maintain that referees are conspiring against Real Madrid is to live in another galaxy," Tebas continued. "That narrative serves as a smokescreen to hide other shortcomings that are plain to see in these opening matches of the season. It is easier to point to a conspiracy than to explain what is actually happening on the pitch.

"A refereeing error does not prove a conspiracy, nor does repeating the claim for years make it true. TIME TO TAKE OFF THE BLINDERS! It is only September, and they are already claiming the league is tainted. No one with common sense buys that old excuse anymore."

With seven games played, Madrid are already six points behind Barcelona, after losing at Real Betis and then in Sunday's derby.

Los Blancos have since responded to Tebas' remarks and appeared to question Tebas' suitability for the role as LaLiga president.

"Our club considers it intolerable for the LaLiga president to use his institutional position to repeatedly disparage and attack Real Madrid in the manner he does during his public statements.

"It is deeply concerning that the person responsible for representing and protecting the interests of all LaLiga clubs remains obsessed with targeting Real Madrid, making our club a constant object of his public attacks."

"Given this persistent and inappropriate behavior, we believe that professional football in Spain urgently needs a leader capable of managing the competition and unlocking its full potential while upholding the fundamental duty of neutrality.

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Liverpool, Arsenal, Man City in race for Feyenoord defender
articles.description: Liverpool are monitoring Feyenoord right back Givairo Read, but face competition from Arsenal and Manchester City. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.body:
Feyenoord right back Givairo Read has caught the eye of Liverpool, Arsenal and Manchester City, while Manchester United are monitoring Borussia Dortmund striker Serhou Guirassy and Vålerenga's 15-year-old winger Gabriel Rajkovic. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Liverpool are monitoring Feyenoord right back Givairo Read, but face competition from Arsenal and Manchester City, according to TEAMtalk. The 20-year-old Netherlands U21 international has registered four assists in seven Eredivisie appearances this season, with all three clubs continuing to track his progress following summer interest. A January move remains an option depending on formal approaches, after Nottingham Forest and AS Roma previously submitted offers of around €20 million that came to nothing.

- Manchester United are monitoring Borussia Dortmund striker Serhou Guirassy as they assess attacking options ahead of January, TEAMtalk reports. The 30-year-old is being considered as an experienced option should Joshua Zirkzee depart, while United remain committed to Benjamin Šeško despite his recent injury issues. Dortmund are reluctant to let Guirassy leave, but his contract has than two years remaining, which could force their hand. Meanwhile, The Sun reports that United are targeting Vålerenga's 15-year-old winger Gabriel Rajkovic as a replacement for JJ Gabriel. 

- Barcelona are monitoring Athletico Paranaense center back Arthur Dias, as per Mundo Deportivo. Barca's head of scouting, João Amaral, reportedly watched the 19-year-old against Bahia, with Tottenham Hotspur, Newcastle United and Atlético Madrid also among his admirers. The left-footed defender, who earned a call-up to Carlo Ancelotti's Brazil squad, has a transfer value of around €30 million and after Spurs previously had a €21 million offer for 80% of his economic rights rejected.

- Tottenham Hotspur will not pursue a move for free-agent Mauro Icardi, Football Insider has revealed. The 33-year-old striker has been available since leaving Galatasaray in July, but Spurs are wary of his wage demands and lack of Premier League experience. Serie A is considered the likeliest destination for the former Sampdoria, Inter Milan and PSG star, with Lazio among several interested Italian clubs.

- Roma are interested in signing free-agent Raphaël Guerreiro, according to Tuttomercatoweb. The 32-year-old Portugal international left back has re-emerged as an option for manager Gian Piero Gasperini as a natural left-footed alternative on the flank, while Olympiacos are also interested in the former Bayern Munich defender.

- Feyenoord midfielder Gjivai Zechiel, 22, is on the radar of Arsenal and Chelsea. (Caught Offside)

- Arsenal could launch a bid for Brentford forward Kevin Schade in January following his strong start to the season. (Ekrem Konur)
